corrections.ruling: A. A fruit card name keeps the second name both source names close with, in one closing bracket, as that name's termbase key and nothing else; N103's purpose — the bracket holds a registered NAME, never a gloss — is met by the bracketed name being a key. The clause 'the whole title a termbase key' binds page titles and is not applied to card names, which are not keys (B would enter fifteen phrases of N281 as names). No gloss, no Urdu name of the fruit and no generic in a card-name bracket (P3c-labels); a source bracket that holds a gloss on either side gives no bracket (N283 C). C refused: it drops names both sources carry. THIS RULING AMENDS THE GUARD OF P3c-labels, as N103 amended it in b7: the guard's 'the one case of item N103' becomes two cases, the second being this one, written into the guard's text (addendum to judge round 2, base_amendments), so that the ruling, its guard and the base guard agree and stand alone. COST, charged: «بن زہیری» (four readers) and «نبق» (two) are unknown words to the reader; neither source explains them.
corrections.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a fruit card name closes with at most one bracket; the bracket holds a termbase key that both source names carry in their closing bracket, and nothing else; P3c-labels' guard carries this as its second case (item N294).
corrections.binds: The card names fruits.g1.f0.name, fruits.g2.f4.name and fruits.g3.f1.name (a bracket each) and fruits.g1.f1.name (no bracket, N283 C); every later fruit or product CARD NAME whose source names close with a bracket. Not other interface headings, labels or section titles: they stay under N103's one case.
fruits.g3.f1.name, fruits.description, fruits.heroSum; later card names only as cases of N294.

base_amendments.guard: As b0-ui's: no bracket in a title, kicker, label or question, save the one case of item N103 of b7 — a title that closes with a single bracket pair holding a second name with which BOTH source titles close in a bracket, the whole title being a termbase key byte for byte, and the second case of item N294 of b18-ui — a fruit card name (an interface heading, not a page title) that closes with a single bracket pair holding a second name with which BOTH source names close in a bracket, that second name being a termbase key byte for byte and nothing else standing in the bracket (the whole card name is not a key); no Urdu generic next to a name that already carries its Arabic generic (a generic after «نامی», in running text, is not next to the name).
